Interstate 25 between Cheyenne and Wheatland was closed to light, high-profile vehicles for over 30 hours. High winds began before midnight March 1st with details in a separate StormData entry for February.

Multiple WYDOT mesonet stations reported high winds with gusts greater than 60 mph. WYDOT mesonet station along Interstate 80 at County Road 402 (WY20) measured maximum wind gust 3 miles east-southeast of Elk Mountain at 10:26 AM MST on the 28th. Interstate 80 between Laramie and Rawlins was closed to light, high-profile vehicles for 27 hours. High winds continued past midnight into March 1st with details in a separate March StormData entry.

Multiple WYDOT mesonet stations reported high winds with gusts 60 to 70 mph. WYDOT mesonet station along Interstate 80 at County Road 402 (WY20) measured maximum wind gust 3 miles east-southeast of Elk Mountain at 2:46 AM MST on the 1st. Interstate 80 between Laramie and Rawlins was closed to light, high-profile vehicles for 27 hours. High winds began before midnight March 1st with details in a separate StormData entry for February.

Observer reported rain turned over to sleet during the overnight hours resulting in a half inch of sleet by early morning of the 5th of March. Also reported a half inch of snow over the half inch of sleet.

Received report at 1053AM MST on the 5th of 8 inches of snow 13 miles south-southeast of Harrison. Additionally, spotter reported 4 inches of snow with near blizzard conditions 18 miles south of Harrison, Nebraska at 1049 AM. Estimated winds at 35 mph on gusts.
Public report of 6 inches of snow 25 miles north northeast of Torrington, Wyoming in southern Sioux County.
Observer reported 6.2 inches of heavy snow on their 8AM CoCoRaHS report. Three other reports were received with 6 inches of snow from Goshen County during event.
Law enforcement in Lusk reported 6 inches of snow in Lusk. A public report was received at 1041 AM of 6 inches of heavy snow in Manville, west of Lusk.
Observer reported 6 inches of heavy snow on their 7AM CoCoRaHS report for 5 March. Numerous reports of heavy snow across east Platte County.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Observer reported 11.2 inches of heavy snow 30 miles southwest of Wheatland on their 7AM CoCoRaHS report.
Report from social media of 9.0 inches of snow 3 miles west of Iron Mountain.
Old Battle SNOTEL (Elev. 10000 ft) reported estimated 12 inches at 1 AM MST on the 6th. Estimated storm total snow of 15 inches.
Medicine Bow SNOTEL (Elev. 10510 ft) estimated 12 inches of snow reached at 11 AM MDT on the 5th. Estimated storm total snow of 13.5 inches.
Douglas Airport ASOS station (KDGW) reported wind chills as low as 36 below zero with air temperatures as low as 20 below zero.
Dixon Airport AWOS station (KDWX) reported wind chills as low as 49 below zero with air temperatures as low as 24 below zero.
Rawlins Airport ASOS station (KRWL) reported wind chills as low as 36 below zero with air temperatures as low as 24 below zero breaking a daily and monthly low temperature record.
Saratoga Airport AWOS station (KSAA) reported wind chills as low as 32 below zero with air temperatures as low as 18 below zero.
Laramie Airport ASOS station (KLAR) reported wind chills as low as 33 below zero with air temperatures as low as 20 below zero breaking a daily low temperature record.
Arlington WYDOT site and Halleck Ridge WYDOT site reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: WYDOT site at Bordeaux on Interstate 25 reported wind gusts in excess of 70 mph through much of the period.

Numerous WYDOT weather sensors along Interstate 80 between Laramie and Rawlins reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph. Maximum wind gust of 76 mph reported at Cooper Cove 7 miles east-southeast of Arlington.
Numerous WYDOT and UPR wind sensors in the South Laramie Range reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
Two WYDOT sites and Emkay UPR site reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
WYDOT site at Bear Creek on Interstate 25 reported continuous wind gusts in excess of 58 mph through the indicated time.
CoCoRaHS and NOHRSC Interpolated Snowfall Analysis Data indicate that 2 to 4 inches of snow fell across primarily western and northern portions of Dawes County.

Extreme wind chills ranging from -30 to -35 degrees F were observed at various stations across Dawes County. The coldest observation was -35 degrees F at the Kings Canyon RAWS near Chadron State Park around 12:00 AM MST on 2/22.
Snowfall accumulations of 4 to 6 inches were reported by multiple NWS COOP Observers across northern Sioux County.
The sensor at Highway 71 along the SD/NE line recorded a minimum wind chill around -35 degrees F which persisted for several hours.
The Alliance Airport ASOS (KAIA) recorded a minimum wind chill of -36 degrees F at 4:00 AM MST on 2/22.
A minimum wind chill of -33 degrees F was observed 11 S of Agate around 3:00 AM MST on 2/22.
A minimum wind chill of -31 degrees F was observed 1 SSW of Scottsbluff at 3:19 AM MST on 2/23.
The AWOS station K1BW located 14 miles west of Harrisburg recorded a minimum wind chill of -30 degrees F at 11:58 PM MST on 2/23.
A minimum wind chill of -32 degrees F was observed at the Kimball Airport (KIBM) at 3:35 AM MST on 2/22.
A Mesonet station located 6 SW of Angora recorded a minimum wind chill of -35 degrees F at 544 AM MST on 2/22.
A minimum wind chill of -37 degrees F was observed at a UPR sensor 3 WNW of Brownson at 5:52 AM MST on 2/22.

The NOHRSC Interpolated Snowfall Analysis and nearby observations along the Niobrara County line suggest that pockets of 3-6 inches of snow fell across western and southeastern portions of the county.
A minimum wind chill of -33 degrees F was observed at a UPR site located 7 WNW of Van Tassel at 3:51 AM MST on 2/22.
Snowfall amounts of 2-4 inches were observed across the lower elevations of Converse County per multiple CoCoRaHS observations.
A minimum wind chill of -32 degrees F was observed at a Mesonet station located at 5 SSW of Douglas at 5:28 AM MST on 2/23.
Widespread snow amounts of 2-4 inches were observed across Goshen County. Localized amounts around 6-8 inches were observed in the far northeast corner of the county south of Van Tassel.
Alliance ASOS reported strong winds during this time.
Charlie site 5 miles northeast of Harrisburg.
Scottsbluff ASOS and RAWS site both reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph during this timeframe.
Railroad sites at 8 west northwest of Bridgeport and 6 east southeast of Bridgeport.
Kimball AWOS site 3 miles south of Kimball.
Sidney airport ASOS along with several railroad sites reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph during event.
Railroad site 2 west northwest of Buford (SHERWS) and Pumpkin Vine WYDOT site.
Several WYDOT sensors reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph during this time.
Laramie airport ASOS reported the peak gust. WYDOT sensor at Quealy Dome also reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
Lone Tree WYDOT site reported highest wind gust. Two other sites hit as well. UPR site at Lynch and WYDOT site at Wildcat Trail hit as well.
Railroad site at EMKAY, 14 miles west southwest of Cheyenne reported the peak gust. Two WYDOT sites hit as well, Wyo Hill and Mile Marker 353.
Bear Creek WYDOT site reported the peak wind gust. Cheyenne ASOS also report a gust to 67 mph at 12:53 PM.
Mesonet site Alpha reported a gust of 58 mph.

events.event_narrative: Bordeaux WYDOT site reported gusts to 58 mph during this time.
Railroad site at Dix2, 1 mile east of Dix reported the peak wind gust. Kimball AWOS also reported several gusts between 58 and 60 mph during this time.
Sidney airport ASOS reported the peak wind. Railroad site at Brown2, 1 west northwest of Brownson and mesonet site 4 north northwest of Brownson also reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
Deer Creek WYDOT site along Interstate 25 reported an extended period of high wind gusts. Douglas Airport ASOS (KDGW) also reported wind gusts to 62 mph.
Van Tassell WYDOT site reported strong wind gusts for an extended period of time.
Esterbrook RAWS site reported maximum wind gust.
Mesonet site at 4 miles west of Muddy Gap in northwest Carbon County.
WYDOT sensor near the zone border reported high winds. WYDOT sensor at Shirley Rim was out for maintenance.
Rawlins ASOS reported the peak gust. Several WYDOT sensors reported wind gusts of 58 mph or greater during this time period.

Coleman WYDOT site along Interstate 25.
Torrington ASOS reported this wind gust.
Cow Creek RAWS site reported this gust.
Skyline WYDOT site reported this wind gust.

Skyline WYDOT site reported this wind gust of 76 mph. This site lays on the southwest border of WYZ114. Roughly 1 mile west of the border.
County Road 402 WYDOT site reported this wind gust. All WYDOT sensors in WYZ110 hit with 60mph or greater wind gusts throughout this event.
Laramie airport ASOS reported this peak gust. Quealy Dome WYDOT site also reported a wind gust to 67mph on 4 April 2022 at 6:04 PM.
Wildcat Trail WYDOT site reported the peak gust.
Railroad site EMKAY reported this peak gust. Several WYDOT sensors reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph during this time as well.
Cheyenne airport ASOS reported this peak wind gust. WYDOT site Bear Creek also reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
Coleman WYDOT site reported this peak gust. Also had reports from Pine Bluffs AWOS of 62 mph and railroad site UP343 of gusts in excess of 58 mph.
Kings Canyon RAWS site reported the peak gust. Chadron airport ASOS also reported numerous gusts of 58 mph or higher.
Alliance airport ASOS reported this gust.
Van Tassell WYDOT site on the Niobrara and North Sioux County line.
Agate RAWS site reported gust to 57 mph at 1113AM.
Scottsbluff RAWS site reported this peak wind gust.
Charlie Mesonet site reported this wind gust.
Lisco NEDOR site on Highway 26 reported this wind gust.
Railroad site UP261 Dix2 reported this wind gust.

Wind chills as low as -30 degrees F were recorded at multiple sensors across Goshen County.
Total snowfall accumulations of 3 to 5 inches were observed across the lower elevations of Platte County. A CoCoRaHS observer reported 5 inches of snow 1 N of Wheatland.

Extreme wind chills occurred across eastern Platte County during the early morning hours on 2/22 and 2/23. The lowest wind chill observed was -34 degrees F at 5:36 AM MST on 2/22, occurring immediately along the Platte/Laramie County line.
Extreme wind chills occurred across eastern Laramie County during the early morning hours on 2/22 and 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -32 degrees F was observed 6 S of Albin at 8:48 AM MST on 2/22.

Extreme wind chills occurred across central Laramie County including the city of Cheyenne during the early morning hours on 2/22 and 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -34 degrees F was observed along the Laramie/Platte County line at 5:36 AM MST.

Multiple sensors across the South Laramie Range Foothills recorded extreme wind chills early in the morning on 2/22, and again during the morning and early afternoon hours on 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -39 degrees F was observed 6 SW of Cheyenne at the WYDOT sensor at Wyo Hill (KWYH).

The Dodge Creek and Esterbrook RAWS sensors in the North Laramie Range both recorded extreme wind chills during the early morning hours on both 2/22 and 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -35 degrees F was observed at Dodge Creek (DODW4) at 7:44 AM MST on 2/23.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A period of light to moderate snow fell across the Central Laramie Range. The interpolated 24-hour snowfall map from NOHRSC ending at 5:00 AM MST on 2/22 suggests peak snowfall totals of 4-6 inches within a narrow band near Bordeaux.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Multiple sensors recorded extreme wind chills as low as -30 degrees F across the Central Laramie Range during the morning hours on both 2/22 and 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -30 degrees was recorded at the WYDOT sensor at Bordeaux (KBRX) at 6:02 AM MST on 2/23.

Numerous sensors recorded wind chills of -35 to -45 degrees F across the South Laramie Range during the morning hours on 2/22, and again through much of the morning and afternoon on 2/23. A minimum wind chill around -46 degrees F was recorded at the WYDOT sensor at Vedauwoo (KVDW) around 6:00 AM MST on 6/23.

Wind chills to -30 degrees F or colder became widespread across the Laramie Valley during the morning hours on both 2/22 and 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -38 degrees F was observed at the Laramie Airport ASOS (KLAR) at 5:20 AM MST on 2/23.
The National Snowfall Analysis from NOHRSC indicated 4-6 inches of snow fell across Northern Carbon County near the Ferris/Seminoe/Shirley Mountains.
A minimum wind chill of -35 degrees F was observed 30 NNE of Rawlins at 1:30 AM MST on 2/23.
A UPR sensor located 2 ESE of Medicine Bow recorded a minimum wind chill of -33 degrees F at 4:16 AM MST on 2/23.

Heavy snow fell across portions of central Carbon County, with an estimated total of 24 inches in the northern foothills of the Sierra Madre mountain range per the Sage Creek Basin SNOTEL at 7850 feet.

Wind chills fell to -30 degrees or lower across portions of Carbon County during the early morning hours on 2/22, and again overnight into 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -37 degrees F was recorded at a Mesonet station 9 W of Rawlins at 10:39 PM MST on 2/22.
A minimum wind chill of -33 degrees F was recorded at the Cow Creek RAWS station at 3:43 AM MST on 2/22.

Various SNOTEL observations reported estimated snowfall totals of 6 to 12 inches, with isolated amounts between 12 to 24 inches. The highest totals in the Sierra Madres were observed at Old Battle (OLDW4) at an elevation of 10000 feet, and Sage Creek Basin (SGBW4) at an elevation of 7850 feet. SWE values were generally over 0.6 inch with an estimated snow-liquid-ratio of 15 to 1.
Wind chills fell below -30 degrees F along the adjacent slopes of the Sierra Madre range.
An official NWS Coop Observer (SFHW4) located 3 N of Saratoga reported a total snowfall of 8.0 inches.
A minimum wind chill of -35 degrees F was observed at the WYDOT sensor at Skyline (KSKL) at 3:52 AM MST on 2/22.
Multiple observations immediately in the vicinity of the foothills of the Snowy Range indicated periods of wind chills to -30 degrees F or less.
A storm total snowfall of around 6 inches was recorded near Elk Mountain by an area CoCoRaHS observer.

Wind chills ranging from -30 to -40 degrees F were common over the North Snowy Range Foothills along the I-80 corridor between Laramie and Rawlins during the early morning hours on both 2/22 and 2/23. A minimum wind chill of -41 degrees F was observed 3 NW of Arlington at 5:52 AM MST on 2/22.
Wind gusts 60-70 MPH were common along the Interstate 80 corridor between Laramie and Rawlins. The peak gust was 78 MPH at the WYDOT sensor at Arlington (KARL) at 1:50 PM MST on 2/19.
Wind gusts briefly reached 58 MPH at Quealy Dome (WY26) along I-80 west of Laramie at 8:08 PM MST on 2/20. The peak gust at the Laramie Airport ASOS (KLAR) was 56 MPH.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Bordeaux Interchange along I-25 between Chugwater and Wheatland experienced frequent gusts of 65 to 75 MPH, with a period of locally extreme wind gusts occurring late in the evening into the early morning hours on 2/20. The peak wind gust at Bordeaux (KBRX) was 99 MPH at 11:08 PM MST on 2/19.
The WYDOT sensor at Coleman (WY1) recorded numerous wind gusts 60-70 MPH with a peak gust to 80 MPH at 11:56 AM MST on 2/19.
Numerous wind gusts 60-70 MPH were observed across the South Laramie Range including the I-80 Summit between Laramie and Cheyenne. The peak wind gust was 77 MPH at UR535 at 11:24 PM MST on 2/19.
Multiple WYDOT and UPR sensors over the South Laramie Range Foothills recorded wind gusts to 60+ MPH. The peak gust was 68 MPH at SPEER3 (UP229) at 2:08 AM MST on 2/20.
The WYDOT sensor at Bear Creek (WY40) along the Laramie/Platte County line recorded frequent gusts 65+ MPH, with a peak gust to 73 MPH at 12:20 AM MST on 2/20.

A brief period of wind gusts around 60 MPH was observed at multiple sensors across eastern Laramie County shortly after Midnight on 2/20. The peak gust was 65 MPH at the WYDOT sensor at Gun Barrel (KGUN) along US-85 at 12:58 AM MST.
A brief wind gust to 59 MPH was observed at the Kimball Airport (KIBM) at 2:55 AM MST on 2/20.
Total snowfall accumulations ranged from 2 to 4 inches across the lower elevations of Converse County per multiple CoCoRaHS observers.
A CoCoRaHS observer 1 S of Lusk reported a storm total snowfall of 4.0 inches.
Total snowfall accumulations ranged from 2 to 4 inches across eastern Platte County per multiple CoCoRaHS observers.
Multiple CoCoRaHS reports of 2 to 3 inches of snowfall around Cheyenne. Highest measurement of 3.2 inches was reported 10 miles east of Cheyenne.
Multiple CoCoRaHS reports of 2 to 4 inches of snowfall across southern Goshen County. Highest measurement of 4.5 inches was reported 3 miles north-northeast of Hawk Springs.
Multiple CoCoRaHS reports of 3.5 inches of snow accumulation near Elk Mountain and 6 miles northeast of Arlington.
Multiple CoCoRaHS reports of 1 to 3 inches of snowfall around Laramie. Highest measurement of 3.3 inches was reported 7 miles south-southeast of Laramie.
CoCoRaHS observer near the Wildcat Hills measured 5 inches of snow accumulation 6 miles south-southeast of Gering.
Multiple CoCoRaHS and COOP observers reported 2 to 3 inches of snow accumulation. Highest snowfall measurement of 3.5 inches was reported by COOP observer 12 miles west-northwest of Harrisburg.

Various SNOTEL observations reported estimated snowfall totals of 5 to 10 inches. The highest totals in the Sierra Madres were observed at Old Battle (OLDW4) at an elevation of 10000 feet with 10.8 inches. SWE values were generally around 0.9 inches with an estimated snow-liquid-ratio of 12 to 1.

Avalanche occurred in the Sierra Madres within the Encampment River Wilderness where a snowmobiler was caught, buried, and killed. The avalanche was triggered by the snowmobiler attempting to climb a steep slope within forested terrain in the vicinity of Green Mountain and the South Fork of Miner Creek.

Cheyenne Airport ASOS station (KCYS) reported one-quarter mile visibility and wind gusts 30 to 35 mph in falling snow for over 10 minutes. Additionally, WYDOT mesonet station Bear Creek (WY40) along Interstate 25 located 8 miles south of Chugwater reported similar conditions lasting for 6 minutes.

Heavy mountain snow was observed in the Sierra Madre mountain range. Multiple SNOTEL observations recorded up to 1.2 inches of SWE with temperatures suggesting ratios between 15 and 20 to 1, resulting in estimated maximum totals of 18 to 24 inches. The highest totals were observed at Old Battle (OLDW4) and Little Snake River (LITW4) at elevations of 10000 and 8915 feet, respectively.

Heavy mountain snow was observed in the Snowy mountain range. Multiple SNOTEL observations recorded up to 1.0 inches of SWE with temperatures suggesting ratios between 15 and 20 to 1, resulting in estimated maximum totals of 15 to 20 inches. The highest totals were observed at Medicine Bow (MBSW4) and Brooklyn Lake (BKLW4) at elevations of 10510 and 10240 feet, respectively.
Multiple CoCoRaHS observers reported 6 to 8 inches of total snowfall near Arlington and Elk Mountain. Interstate 80 was closed between Laramie and Rawlins due to winter conditions.

Total snowfall ranged from 3 to 6 inches across Shirley Basin, per estimates from the NOHRSC Interpolated Snowfall Analysis. Wyoming Route 487 was closed from Medicine Bow to Wyoming Route 220 due to winter conditions.
The Windy Peak SNOTEL in the North Laramie Range (WNDW4) recorded an estimated storm total snowfall of 14 inches, based on 0.7 inch of SWE and an estimated ratio of 20 to 1.
A CoCoRaHS observer 4 WSW of Douglas recorded a storm total snowfall of 4.0 inches.
Multiple observers across central Carbon County recorded storm total snowfall accumulations of 4 to 6 inches.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Multiple reports of 6 to 8 inches of snow were received across the central Laramie Range south and west of Wheatland.

An estimated storm total snowfall of 8.0 inches was recorded at the Crow Creek SNOTEL in the South Laramie Range (CRWW4). This was based on an SWE of 0.4 inch and a snow ratio of approximately 20 to 1. In addition, Interstate 80 was closed between Laramie and Cheyenne due to winter conditions.

A CoCoRaHS observer 11 miles NW of Cheyenne in the South Laramie Range Foothills recorded a storm total snowfall of 6.5 inches. In addition, Interstate 80 was closed between Laramie and Cheyenne due to winter conditions.
The general public reported a storm total snowfall of 6.0 inches in Chugwater.
Multiple observers reported 4 to 6 inches of snowfall across central Laramie County. Interstate 80 was closed between Cheyenne and Laramie due to winter conditions.
Widespread snowfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches were observed across Goshen County. The public reported an isolated total of 6.0 inches 4 W of Hawk Springs.
The public reported 8.0 inches of snow in Pine Bluffs.
An official NWS Co-Op observer reported 5.2 inches of snow 9 WSW of Harrison in Northern Sioux County.
A swath of 4 to 5 inches of snow fell across the Platte River Valley in Scotts Bluff county from Morrill to Scottsbluff and Gering.
An official NWS Co-Op observer reported 5.2 inches of snow along the Morrill/Banner county line.

The NOHRSC Interpolated Snowfall Analysis indicated a swath of 6+ inches of snow fell across far southeastern Banner County. An official NWS Co-Op observer reported 5.2 inches of snow immediately along the Banner/Morrill County line 18 WNW of Bridgeport.
The public reported 9.0 inches of snow in Kimball.
Multiple observers reported 6 to 8 inches of snow across Cheyenne County. The public reported 8.0 inches of snow in Sidney.
An official NWS Co-Op observer reported 5.2 inches of snow just east of Van Tassel along the Niobrara/Sioux County Line.

events.cz_name: CENTRAL LARAMIE RANGE AND SOUTHWEST PLATTE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: WYDOT mesonet station Bordeaux (KBRX) along Interstate 25 measured maximum wind gust 9 miles south of Wheatland at 5:34 AM MDT. Interstate 25 between Cheyenne and Wheatland was closed to light, high profile vehicles for over 12 hours.

Multiple WYDOT mesonet stations reported high winds along Interstate 80 between Laramie and Rawlins. WYDOT mesonet station at Elk Mountain (WY19) measured maximum wind gust at 7:06 AM MDT. Interstate 80 between Laramie and Rawlins was closed to light, high profile vehicles for 10 hours.

WYDOT mesonet station along Interstate 80 at Lone Tree (WY36) measured wind gusts to 59 mph. Additionally, Union Pacific Railroad mesonet station SHERWS (UR535) measured maximum wind gust 2 miles west-northwest of Buford.

WYDOT mesonet station along Interstate 80 at mile marker 353 (WY39) measured wind gusts of 58 mph. Additionally, Union Pacific Railroad mesonet station EMKAYW (UP226) measured maximum wind gust 14 miles west-southwest of Cheyenne.

Cheyenne Airport ASOS station (KCYS) reported high winds with gusts up to 62 mph. Additionally, multiple WYDOT mesonet stations reported high winds with Bear Creek (WY40) along Interstate 25 measuring the maximum wind gusts 8 miles south of Chugwater at 12:18 PM MDT.

Old Battle SNOTEL (Elev. 10000 ft) estimated 13.5 inches of snowfall with 0.9 inches of snow water equivalent and 15:1 snow ratios. Additional SNOTELs in the area estimated 9 to 12 inches of snow accumulation.
Area SNOTELs estimated 6 to 10 inches of snow accumulation with higher amounts along the western slopes of the Snowy Range.

Scattered snow showers in the Arlington and Elk Mountain areas with brief reductions to visibility and light snowfall accumulations resulting in multiple accidents along Interstate 80 between Laramie and Rawlins. A supercell thunderstorm developed east of Lusk, WY near 2PM MDT on|7 June 2022 north of Highway 20 that exhibited broad rotation from|KCYS radar. This rotation tightened near 2:20pm MDT just north of|Highway 20 west-northwest of Duck Creek Ranch. First indications of|ground damage start at west side of Duck Creek Ranch with wood fencing|blown down. The tornado intensified and widened as it approached|Duck Creek Ranch with metal sheeting fencing pulled from metal|posts and roof damage occurring on a large ranch shed. A|convergent damage pattern was apparent with the debris of the wood|fencing being blown west and the solid sheet metal fencing blown|north and bent backwards to the west with the roof damage facing|south. Hardwood trees were snapped at the base along with softwood|pines both snapped and uprooted in proximity to a single family|home. The snapped pine tree and the uprooted pine tree were facing|opposite directions. The more impressive damage was a barn roof|and partial second level were torn off and thrown 50 to 100 yards|to the southeast. Additional tin roof peeling damage was noted on|another farm building and a large side sheet metal and wood|section on the southern end of the tornado path was torn from the|facade. Duck Creek Ranch is where the more intense damage was|noted. Farther southeast along, Highway 20, sporadic pockets of|cattle windbreak fencing damage was noted near a WYDOT road sensor|that gusted to 78mph during this time frame. Lastly, near mile|marker 59 on Highway 20, four (4) power poles were leaning south|and marks the end of the tornado path. No additional damage was|seen or reported in Van Tassell and along South Van Tassell Road.

The same tornado tracked to the southeast and damaged another outbuilding and a barn 3 miles southeast of Hawk Springs. The tornado was officially rated an EF-2. A confirmed tornado began approximately 12 miles W of Albin at 6:42 PM MDT. The tornado damaged a single-family residence and destroyed a farm outbuilding. Minimal shingle damage was was visible at the home, with trees and power lines remaining intact on the property. Debris from the home and outbuilding was thrown several hundred yards to the southeast. Hay bales weighing up to 1400 pounds were moved between one quarter and one half mile from their original location. Further southeast along the track of the tornado, 8 wooden power poles were snapped. The damage then became more sporadic along the track as the tornado moved over mainly open fields before dissipating approximately 9 miles WSW of Albin at 6:50 PM MDT.

A supercell first developed over Laramie County in southeast Wyoming|dropping golf ball to baseball size hail while exhibiting mid-level|rotation. The supercell was long lived and made its way into Kimball|County, Nebraska where it began to show tornadic structure. Based off|of radar and storm spotter reports, the estimated start point is just|southeast of the intersection of County Road 29 and 14 at around 6:35|PM MDT. The tornado tracked south-southeast, remaining mainly over|open farmland, kicking up large amounts of dirt and dust. As the|tornado tracked south-southeast it eventually crossed County Road|10 between County Road 29 and 33. At this site, there was very|little damage aside from an insulator cap blown away and a loose|wire on an electrical pole. The tornado continued travailing to|the southeast on County Road 35, north of County Road 6, where|it caused minor damage to a farmhouse and the surrounding barns|on the property. Tree limbs 1 to 3 inches in diameter were broken|and scattered across the property. A few shingles were torn off|the farmhouse, an augur was pushed approximately 5 feet to the|southwest digging a groove in the soil, and a calving hut was|blown 20 feet and rotated about 100 degrees. A few hundred|yards south down County Road 35 an electrical pole roughly 50|years old was snapped at the base but still upright as it was|still attached to the electrical wires. A plastic 5 gallon bucket|from the farmhouse was thrown about half a mile away from the|home in a field off of County Road 6. Finally, the tornado|dissipated over an open field just to the west of Highway 71,|about 2 miles southeast of the farmhouse at 6:45 PM MDT.|Overall, damage seen was consistent with that of an EF-0 tornado|with maximum winds of 80 to 85 MPH.

At approximately 6:47 PM, video evidence from multiple sources|shows a satellite tornado formed to the northeast of the original|tornado after it dissipated. This tornado lasted about 1 to 2|minutes and remained over open farmland near the intersection|of County Road 10 and 31. No damage was reported, therefore the|tornado is classified as an EF-U.

A brief tornado was observed in rural Goshen County by numerous storm spotters|and emergency management personnel. Due to the rural nature of this tornado, only|limited damage to fencing was found, as well as scattered plant debris. Review of|video and photo sequences along with radar time-matching indicate that this tornado|likely began as a landspout, but quickly gained mesocyclonic characteristics as it|interacted with the updraft base, condensed a funnel, and slowed/occluded into the|storm. Regardless, without any damage of note this tornado will be recorded as EF-U.

An NWS damage survey found evidence of EF-1 tornado damage at multiple|properties along County Road D as well as along Highway 26. One residence|had partial roof structure failure as well as roofing material completely|removed. Another garage facility experienced total structural collapse and|foundation shift. Numerous large tree limbs 1-2 feet in diameter were snapped|and scattered. Several smaller metal outbuildings were also destroyed and scattered.||Of important note, this tornado occurred along the northern fringe of a much|larger area of powerful straight-line outflow winds observed in excess of 90|to 100 mph. Damage indicators from the straight-line winds throughout Scotts Bluff|county were all pointed eastward. This was in dramatic contrast to the tornado|path which featured a chaotic scattering of damage and debris, some of which|was lofted north and even back west of the circulation path.

events.event_narrative: Persistent three day wind event reported at the Bordeaux WYDOT sensor along Interstate 80. Peak wind gust of 79 MPH was reported at 836 AM on March 8th. This resulting in a long duration shutdown of Interstate 25 for high profile vehicles.
Nine out of thirteen WYDOT sites reported persistent wind gusts over 58 MPH from March 7th through March 9th. Peak gust of 71 MPH was observed at Foote Creek, near Arlington along Interstate 80.
Three observation sites reported peak wind gusts of 59 and 60 MPH. Peak gust of 60 MPH was observed at Curt Gowdy State Park.
A few sites reported high sustained winds between 40 to 46 MPH for more than one hour. Peak wind gust of 59 MPH was reported at Otto Road along Interstate 80 at 926 AM on March 8th.

Two reports of storm total snowfall of 7 inches and 10.1 inches at Elk Mountain and near Rock River, respectively. Locally heavy banded snow impacted a small part of the region, resulting in locally high snow accumulations. Interstate 80 closed west of Laramie due to snow packed roads and accidents.
Three inches of snow reported near Encampment, in the North Platte River Valley.
Six to nine inches of snow reported across the Snowy Range.

Elk Mountain snow observers reported snow accumulations between 3 to 4 inches along Interstate 80.
A few WYDOT sites reported gusts over 58 MPH for a few hours. The peak gust of 64 MPH was measured at Halleck Ridge along Interstate 80.

Strong wind gusts between 65 to 75 MPH was observed at most observation stations across the lower elevations of Converse County. Peak gust of 75 MPH reported at Douglas Airport ASOS and a mesonet sensor southwest of town, and 77 MPH southwest of Glenrock.

A peak gust of 75 MPH was reported near Muddy Gap Junction.

events.event_narrative: Frequent very strong winds were observed at the WYDOT site at Bordeaux. Highest gust observed at 126 PM MST on March 12th. Several webcam images showed flipped semi trucks on Interstate 25.

Most observation sites in eastern Platte County reported wind gusts over 58 MPH. The public reported and sent a photo of an uprooted tree and several downed power lines in Wheatland Wyoming. Peak gust of 76 MPH was measured at the Coleman WYDOT site north of Wheatland while Wheatland Airfield measured a gust of 63 MPH.
Occasional strong wind gusts over 58 MPH reported across a few observation sites over Goshen County. Peak gust of 72 MPH measured at Torrington Airport later in the afternoon.

Seven observation sites across central Carbon County reported strong wind gusts over 58 MPH in a long duration high wind event. Peak gust of 75 MPH measured at the WYDOT site at Sinclair, east of Rawlins. Rawlins Airport measured a peak gust of 70 MPH late in the morning on March 12th.

All reporting observation sites across the northern Snowy Range Foothills measured persistent wind gusts over 58 MPH in a long duration wind event. Peak wind gust of 97 MPH was measured at Cooper Cove, northwest of Laramie.
Intermittent strong wind gusts reported at Saratoga and south of Saratoga near the Colorado border. Peak gust of 63 MPH measured at the WYDOT site in Skyline.

Personal weather station near Lake Hattie Reservoir reported a peak gust of 109 MPH fifteen miles west southwest of Laramie. Herrick Lane WYDOT site reported a peak wind gust 93 MPH along Interstate 80 northwest of Laramie, and Laramie Airport reported a peak wind gust 81 MPH.
WYDOT webcam in Laramie showed blowing dust with visibilities between one quarter to one half mile along Interstate 80.

Most observation sites across the southern Laramie Range reported persistent wind gusts over 58 MPH over a long duration wind event. Peak gust of 90 MPH was measured at the Union Pacific Railroad site at LYNCHW, near Buford.
Webcam at Vedauwoo shows visibility below one quarter of a mile in blowing dust.

All observation sites west of Cheyenne reported persistent strong wind gusts over 58 MPH. Peak wind gust of 96 MPH measured at the EMKAYW Union Pacific Railroad site. Numerous photos of at least three flipped over semi trucks on Interstate 25 near the Colorado border.

Long duration damaging high wind event for central Laramie County, including all of Cheyenne. Numerous reports of downed/uprooted trees, widespread power outages which impacted the city of Cheyenne and surrounding areas, damaged fences, personal property damage. A few reports of very large trees uprooted around the older parts of the city, including 29th and Carey, near the Cheyenne Public Library. Numerous reports and webcam images of flipped over semi trucks with minor injuries near the junction of Interstate 25 and Interstate 80. Peak gust of 109 MPH measured at the Bear Creek WYDOT site. Cheyenne Airport ASOS measured a peak gust of 92 MPH.
Several reports of persistent strong wind gusts over 58 MPH over eastern Laramie County. Peak gust of 81 MPH measured at the WYDOT site at Gun Barrel, along US Highway 85.

A few strong wind gusts were measured at Alliance Airport. Peak wind gust of 71 MPH was observed in the middle of the afternoon.

A storm damage survey team from the National Weather Service in Cheyenne confirmed an EF-1 tornado touched down in eastern Scotts Bluff County on Monday evening June 7th, 2010.  Additionally, some of the damage was attributed to strong straight-line thunderstorm winds.  Baseball sized hail accompanied this tornadic thunderstorm.| |Based on the survey and interviews with area residents, an EF-1 tornado touched down on the east side of the city of Scottsbluff. An automotive dealership sustained roof damage. Five mobile home trailers were over-turned in the Wagon Wheel Trailer Park. An outbuilding collapsed and a metal shed sustained substantial roof damage 2.4 miles southeast of Scottsbluff along County Road 24. A roof was torn off a garage and numerous trees were uprooted south of Highway 26, 5.4 miles southeast of Scottsbluff. Four grain bins were removed from their foundations in the town of Melbeta. One of the grain bins was lifted one half mile from its foundation. Based on this damage it was determined that the tornado path consisted of numerous spin-ups over the 19-mile damage path. The tornado finally dissipated just north of Chimney Rock at around 8 pm.||The damage to the mobile homes...trees north of Melbeta...and the grain bins were consistent with EF-1 tornado damage with winds estimated to be in the 93 to 98 mph range.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain moved across the Snowy Range and Brush Creek area on State Highway 130 between 9 pm and midnight on July 18.  Debris carried down Brush Creek by runoff from the heavy rainfall clogged the drainage culvert at milepost 55.8 on State Highway 130, about 13 miles east of the junction with State Highway 230.  As a result, water washed away the pavement around the culvert and created a 25-foot wide, 9-foot deep trench in the road just before 1 am on July 19.  Four members of a Colorado Springs family died after their van drove into the washout and was swept downstream by the raging creek as they fled flash flooding at a nearby campground shortly after 1 am.  The driver of the van managed to escape from the van, which was submerged to its rooftop.  Minutes later, the Carbon County emergency manager who responded to the flash flooding, drove his vehicle into the same washout and plunged into the creek.  Firefighters rescued both drivers about two hours later, and were transported to a hospital in Rawlins.  Both men were treated for their injuries and later released.  After floodwaters receded, State Highway 130 between mileposts 36 and 68 was closed for repairs.

A large tornado touched down west of Wheatland and moved to the southeast across western Platte County.  The tornado remained in contact with the ground for just over an hour before dissipating northeast of Chugwater.  An NWS survey team rated the tornado an EF2 with maximum winds estimated between 130 and 135 mph.  The damage assessment revealed the most significant damage to be along Olson Road, about 6 miles southwest of Wheatland.  An unoccupied mobile home was completely destroyed, with unrecognizable debris spread about 50 yards from the foundation.  A poorly constructed modular home with a crawl space was completely swept from its foundation, with parts of the metal frame found one quarter of a mile away.  Many outbuildings on various properties were severely damaged or completely destroyed.  A well-constructed one to two family home lost a large portion of the roof, but most of the walls remained intact with the exception of the garage.  The most significant damage, however, was found near the intersection of Grange and Olson Roads.  A very well constructed and recently completed barn was demolished, with debris found more than two miles away.  In addition to the building damage, numerous large cottonwood trees were either snapped or uprooted but were not debarked.  The tornado also derailed 6 empty rail cars about 6 miles northeast of Chugwater, shortly before it dissipated.  The tornado crossed Interstate 25 just south of the Bordeaux exit at about 14:38 MST.  No vehicles were affected by the tornado as it crossed the interstate.  One person suffered minor injury from flying debris.

The National Weather Service in Cheyenne rated the June 11 2013 Dawes County Nebraska tornado as EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale with maximum 3 second wind gusts of 110 mph.  The tornado touched down 19 miles south-southwest of Chadron, just west of the T intersection of Hough Road. The tornado moved east, then slightly southeast, dissipating seven minutes later just north of Hough Road.  The damage path length and width were  estimated at one mile and 40 yards, respectively.  At least 16 structures were damaged, with at least eight outbuildings destroyed.  Numerous trees and telephone poles were snapped and two horse trailers were thrown several hundred feet.  Two distinct swirl marks were located along the damage path, estimated around 12 feet in diameter.  The supercell thunderstorm associated with the tornado produced very little rain or hail, but several cloud to ground lightning strikes near the tornado.

A storm survey team from the National Weather Service in Cheyenne rated the June 22 2013 Banner County Nebraska tornado as a EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale with maximum three second wind gusts of 100 mph.  The tornado, which developed from a high precipitation supercell thunderstorm, touched down about 17 miles west-northwest of Harrisburg Nebraska.  The tornado moved to the east-southeast for several miles before dissipating about 10 miles northwest of Harrisburg.  A total of eight structures were damaged with at least one outbuilding destroyed.  The outbuilding was supported by large wooden planks about six inches thick...most of which were snapped at the center.  The roof was removed from a three stall garage but all of the walls remained intact.  A two-story hone was damaged by flying debris, with a 2 X 4 inch plank driven through the second floor wall by the tornadic winds.  Sheet metal and wooden boards from damaged outbuildings were found 50 to 100 yards to the northwest in a shelter belt.  Multiple other structures suffered roof damage with sections of sheet metal peeled off.  Six power poles were snapped near the touchdown site with another damaged east of Stegall Road.  Several six to 12 inch diameter hardwood trees were also snapped.  Center pivots were either flipped or twisted in multiple directions along the tornado's path.

Semitrailers traveling east on Interstate 80 were among 70 vehicles involved in three separate pileups that occurred at mile marker 342, about 20 miles west of Cheyenne near the Harriman Road exit. Very low visibility in dense fog and icy road surface contributed to a deadly, multi-vehicle pileup on Interstate 80 18 miles west of Laramie at mile marker 292 about 8 am.  A 22,000 gallon tanker was on fire.  Interstate 80 and nearby highways 30 and 287 were closed.  WYDOT posted Speeds Advised at 45 MPH and Black Ice Advisory In Effect on their interstate signs.  As many as 25 motorists were injured and two were killed in the pileup.

The EF1 tornado touched down four miles east of Yoder near Highway 161 and moved northeast at 30 mph.  Much of the damage was observed along County Road 157 and Highway 92 south of Torrington.  The tornado damaged the roof of a Holiday Inn Express hotel on East Valley Road in Torrington, uprooted trees, destroyed power lines and traffic lights.  A barn was destroyed with sheet metal and wood blown 30 yards away.  The nearby home's shingle roof was damaged.  The tornado lifted 25 minutes later about a mile east of Torrington. Four to six inches of rain from a stationary thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding across southwest Niobrara County.  Highway 20 from Keeline to Manville was inundated with several feet of water.  A culvert on Highway 20 near Manville was washed out.  Law enforcement officials evacuated residents in Manville as well as along the swollen Niobrara River near Manville.

As much as eight inches of rain fell from slow moving thunderstorms across south and southeast Niobrara County during the predawn hours, which resulted in widespread flash flooding.  Excessive runoff upstream into the Niobrara River and nearby creeks caused them to overflow their banks.  Law enforcement officials evacuated residents of Lusk as well as those living along the Niobrara River downstream to Van Tassel several hours in advance of the flood wave.  The worst damage occurred in Lusk where 20 to 30 homes and 15 to 20 businesses were destroyed.  Flood waters and debris rushed down Main Street in Lusk, swamped four blocks, and shut down the town's water supply.  The US Highway 85 bridge on the north side of Lusk collapsed onto the railroad tracks below.  Flash flooding closed a 20-mile stretch of US Highway 20 from Lusk to the Nebraska border, US Highway 85 from Lusk to the Goshen County line, and a 35-mile stretch of Highway 270 from Manville north to Lance Creek. WYDOT closed traffic into and out of Lusk, except for residents and emergency responders.  Various state agencies, including the Red Cross and Wyoming National Guard, assisted in the flood cleanup efforts.  A local command center was established at the Lusk Fairgrounds with water, food and shelter.  The governor declared a state of emergency for Niobrara County.  Fortunately, there were no injuries or fatalities.

A brief tornado touchdown occurred 11 miles northeast of Cheyenne approximately 1.25 miles southeast of the intersection of Highway 85 and CR 222.  This tornado moved north causing damage to irrigation center pivot, windows, roof, and outbuildings of one rural residence (DI 4, DOD 4). The tornado moved across US Highway 85 and lifted approximately 1.75 miles northeast of the intersection of Highway 85 and CR 222.

The tornado crossed into southern Laramie County, Wyoming from Weld County, Colorado approximately 4 miles southeast of Carpenter. It continued moving towards the north-northwest crossing mostly open farmland, paralleling County Road 151 where it impacted 4 residences. The most significant damage observed by the NWS assessment team was to 2 residences along County Road 151, where a semi-attached garage was completely destroyed (DI 1, DOD 3) by EF-2 intensity winds. Damage also was observed to single family roof structure. Additionally, numerous power poles were snapped along with a ruptured power line.

A short-lived tornado touched down just north of the Colorado state line to the southwest of Pine Bluffs along County Road 161. It was on the ground for approximately 4-7 minutes. A fifth-wheel horse trailer was lofted into the air for 50 yards sustaining significant damage. A small farm outbuilding was also destroyed (DI 1, DOD 7).

A brief tornado touched down along County Road 17 approximately 9 miles north of Bushnell, NE. A roof of an old barn was torn off and exterior walls collapsed (DI 1, DOD 6). An auger cart and auger were tipped. Power poles broke near the farm.

A short-lived tornado touched down east of Highway 71 southeast of Harrisburg, NE. A calving barn was moved about 10 yards from its original location. One horse was killed with several other horses injured. Several power poles were broken. A grain bin was pushed off its foundation, landing east into grove of trees. Pole barn rolled with only a few walls left standing (DI 1, DOD 7).

Storm chasers captured video of a tornado briefly touching down in a remote section of southern Banner County. The tornado caused no damage from which the NWS could assign an EF-scale rating. Path was estimated by cross-referencing storm chaser reports and radar data.

Storm chasers captured video of a tornado briefly touching down about 15 miles west-northwest of Chadron, NE in Dawes County. The location was estimated based on video and radar data. The tornado caused no damage from which the NWS could assign an EF-scale rating.

Emergency management, an off-duty NWS employee, and storm chasers observed a series of tornado touchdowns in rural western Goshen County. The tornado path was discontinuous with no damage from which the NWS could assign an EF-scale rating.
A brief tornado spin-up occurred along Cold Springs Road southwest of Douglas. An outbuilding was completely destroyed (DI 1, DOD 8).

A brief tornado touched down on the east side of Bayard, NE producing damage consistent of EF-1 (DI 17, DOD 3) to the Chimney Rock Villa Nursing Home. The tornado lifted quickly as it moved east of Bayard. Many irrigation pivots overturned within 1-2 miles west of Bayard, as well as damage on the west side of town consistent with damaging straight-line winds.

A long-track discontinuous tornado path was surveyed by the NWS damage team, initially touching down northwest of the Highway 26 and L62A intersection, 4 miles north-northwest of Bayard, NE. The tornado continued east along and north of L62A. Significant damage consistent of EF-2 tornadic damage was surveyed at a farmhouse approximately 6 miles northeast of Bayard. The house was severely damaged with the roof taken off and numerous exterior walls destroyed (DI 4, DOD 8). A detached garage was swept clean (DI 1, DOD 8) with several trucks slid from their original location. A flat bed and horse trailer were lofted 100 yards from their original position. Trees to the west of the residence were denuded. This storm produced additional damage some of which was due to straight-line winds along L62A. This damage included damage to a steel farm outbuilding, rolled mobile home, rolled semi tractor trailer, rolled center pivots, and continued tree denuding. The storm lifted northeast near Highway 385 with additional damage surveyed at Angora, including downed power poles and a train derailment. The discontinuous tornado continued northeast exiting Morrill County near Highway 385 by 1904 MST. This storm continued and produced additional damage in Box Butte County.

A discontinuous tornado path continued northeast into Box Butte County from Morrill County. Additional roof damage was surveyed to a large building near the Alliance Airport (DI 1, DOD 3). This was the end of the discontinuous tornado path in Morrill and Box Butte Counties. Sixty-five train cars were blown over south of Alliance.

Significant tornado damage was noted at a ranch 20 miles north-northeast of Torrington, WY, just west of the Union Pacific railway line. Significant damage consistent with EF-2 intensity winds was to the main ranch residence and surrounding barns (DI 1, DOD 8). Several three-quarter ton pickup trucks were vaulted several yards by tornadic winds, with several horse trailers rolled 50 to 100 yards and severely damaged. Several horses at this location were seriously injured with 3 horses killed. One person in the residence received minor head injuries. The tornado continued northeast, moving into Sioux County, NE at 1630 MST.

A tornado crossed the WY/NE state line into Sioux County, NE at 1630 MST, and continued northeast before lifting west of Highway 29, 8 miles south-southwest of Harrison, NE at 1701 MST. Damage consistent with EF-2 intensity was noted by the survey team to the residence, as well as to surrounding trees and outbuildings (DI 2, DOD 6) 13 miles southwest of Harrison, NE. One resident at this location was treated and released at a local hospital with injuries incurred from flying debris in the home.

The first observed evidence of the tornado was near Rattlesnake Hill just north of Wagonhound Road.  The tornado moved to the south and quickly grew stronger.  The NWS survey team continued to investigate some video evidence that the tornado may have been on the ground prior to Rattlesnake Hill.  The tornado snapped several trees and power poles along Wagonhound Road, and blew several large rolls of hay nearly 300 yards from a large hay bale stack.   The tornado intensified as it moved south toward a ranch, reaching EF3 intensity through the barn and residence, destroying several buildings and causing significant damage to the ranch house.  The ranch house had large sections of roof structure removed, and a quonset hut tractor storage area just west of the house was destroyed.  Two large utility trailers weighing several thousand pounds were lofted and had not been located, with the exception of one axel set.  Large cottonwood trees were stripped of all vegetation with just the largest limbs near the center of the trees remaining intact.  The tornado continued south-southeast before lifting in the vicinity of Poison Lake.  Start and end and locations and times of the tornado were estimated from eyewitness accounts and radar data.

The second tornado formed as the first tornado was lifting to the west, touching down near the West Fork of La Bonte Creek and Esterbrook Road.  The tornado quickly strengthened to EF1 intensity as it moved along La Bonte Creek passing near a ranch house off Esterbrook Road.  Most of the damage was to trees that were snapped mid trunk in a 150 yard path.  The tornado lifted as it moved east of La Bonte Creek.  The NWS survey team lost track of the tornado as it  moved southeast into open country, so it is possible that track extended farther than the survey results indicated.  The survey team also continued to investigate reports of damage at Esterbrook Campground to the southeast, to see if this damage was associated with the same tornado.  Start and end times and locations and times of the tornado were estimated from eyewitness accounts and radar data.

events.event_narrative: A lightning strike in the vicinity of Britania Mountain sparked a wildfire that grew across portions of Albany and Platte Counties. An isolated supercell thunderstorm developed a tornado three to four miles west of Highway 30. The tornado continued an eastward track and intensified rapidly over the mainly open fields. Numerous wooden power poles were snapped along County Road 121, along with several galvanized steel utility poles, which were bent 90 degrees at the base. Grass was scoured out of the ground in a wide swath approximately one third of a mile in width near the intersection of County Road 121 and Cattle drive. The observed tornado continued east into the Laramie Range near King Mountain Road.

A satellite tornado formed two miles to the south of the parent tornado. The tornado damaged treetops and caused significant structural damage to a well-built attached garage, which collapsed as it lifted off the foundation and shifted to the east. In addition, several nearby structures had minor damage to siding and shingles as the tornado was observed moving through the Antelope Ridge Loop subdivision, six miles north of Laramie, and into open country.
The large hail caused damage to cars and trailers in the Pole Mountain area.

Significant tornado damage was noted near Federal, Wyoming where eight structures were impacted along Mountain Shadow Drive and Mountain Shadow Lane. The tornado initially touched down just northeast of Federal, tracking south, before lifting south of Federal. Significant damage consistent with a EF-2 tornado was observed to a manufactured home just east of Federal, where the roof had been removed, garage destroyed, while exterior walls were left attached to the foundation and intact. The tornado continued south tossing numerous livestock and camper trailers. High-end EF-2 damage was observed to a single family residence farther south, where the roof and a few exterior walls were removed. A garage and exterior shed was also destroyed at the residence. The tornado continued south removing the roof of another home half a miles southeast of Federal. Numerous damage to roofs around the area was also noted.
A car was damaged near the Whitaker exit along Interstate 25 with clear indication of tornado rotation. Without a damage indicator, however, this portion of the tornado was rated EF-Unknown.

A supercell thunderstorm developed near the town of Rock River, Wyoming, in west-central Albany County.  At 606 PM MDT, the storm rapidly intensified as it moved southeast.  A tornado touched down and crossed Highway 30 south of Bosler, Wyoming at 610 PM MDT, and dissipated at 619 PM MDT.  The storm continued to show signs of rotation as it moved east-southeast toward the Laramie County line, however no additional tornadoes were reported.||A survey team from the National Weather Service in Cheyenne met with officials from Albany County to investigate storm damage in the Bosler area.  Eyewitness reports and snapped wooden power poles along County Road 51 indicated the initial tornado touched down in an open field about 2.5 miles west-southwest of Bosler, or 18.5 miles north-northwest of Laramie.  The tornado lifted for a short time but descended again and caused complete destruction of a pole barn near Highway 30 about three miles south-southeast of Bosler.  The tornado crossed Highway 30, confirmed by aerial photographs provided by the City of Laramie.  Large pieces of warped metal were blown several hundred yards to the east of the highway in a wide swath.  The damage footprint ended near the point of the original report.  Damage was consistent with an EF-1 tornado with maximum winds around 100 mph.

Numerous reports |of funnels from chasers and storm spotters were received just after 5pm MDT. Much stronger low-level rotation developed near 5:14pm MDT via KCYS radar with confirmed tornado touchdown occurring at 5:15pm MDT. The touchdown occurred 3 miles west of |Interstate 25 west of mile marker 49. The cone tornado was observed on the ground via live-stream, pictures, and video through numerous social media channels. Tornado remained west of Interstate 25 through the entirety of its life cycle as it roped out about 1 mile west of the interstate over open ranch land. Time of dissipation is near 5:30pm MDT. During the course of the tornadic supercell thunderstorm, several storm chasers and emergency managers were reporting the sighting of a wedge-shaped tornado moving across the high plains. During the lifetime of the tornado, videos submitted to the office referenced multi-vortex tornadoes and various satellite tornadoes as it neared and eventually passed over United States Highway 85. Several buildings were damaged in the path of the twister along with various lifestock and wild animals killed by flying debris. Damage at one of the residences was equivalent to EF-2 damage. Given the sparse and remote areas that the tornado passed through, path length and width are at best an estimate given that the tornado path was discontinuous and at time impossible to investigate given private land and no road access.

A gentleman traveling through the area crashed his vehicle on the afternoon of the 25th during heavy snowfall in the area along state highway 70 near Dixon. The vehicle as a result of the crash caught on fire with the driver becoming lost after walking away. Crews were unable to locate the driver due to the inclement weather resulting in his body being found in a ravine a mile and a half from the crash the next morning. Coroner reports death was due to exposure from the elements with snowfall and temperatures in the 20s. A Quasi-Linear Convective System (QLCS) with an embedded supercell structure|developed across far SE Carbon County around 2:45pm on 6/6/2020, and moved|across western and northern portions of the Snowy Mountain Range. The overall|radar presentation of the co-located cyclonic rotation at the leading edge of|the reflectivity surge improved near 2:50-2:56pm per the radar scans from KCYS.|The first note of tree damage from the tornado occurred on Forest Service Road 115 |(FS115) that ran west of the main Forest Service Road 100 (FS100) at an elevation |around 9200 feet. Sporadic softwood pine trees were uprooted along FS115 and fell to |the N/NW direction. The survey team continued north on FS100, and additional tree |branches and smaller pine trees were uprooted. Progressing farther north along FS100, |tree damage became more widespread and severe with degree of damage indicators increasing |as more snapped softwood pine trees were cataloged and noted. This portion of FS100 |decreases in elevation and into a narrow localized valley along Turpin Creek to the north |and northwest. A vantage point at the south end of the valley, higher in elevation,|allowed for a landscape view towards the main tree damage path. This enhanced visual|perspective allowed the survey team to see east-northeast uprooted and bent|softwood pine trees. There were also snapped pine trees down the main center line of the damage path oriented to the north to north-northwest, and softwood pine trees to the east of the main centerline, converging back to the west to northwest. It was noted the greatest tree damage on the south to middle portions of the local Turpin Creek Valley. This damage was located along the west side of FS100, crossed FS100, with the greatest snapping to the East as one progressed farther north along FS100. This evidence indicated the tornado crossed FS100 in following the main snapping of tree damage along with the notable convergent pattern of tree fall. From the south side of the local Valley, tree damage extended at least 100-200 yards west of the road, with a wider damage swath noted to the east of FS100 as one progressed farther north. The damage swath of uprooted and snapped trees east of FS100 was approximately 200-300 yards from the road. The damage area narrowed substantially and became indiscernible as the team progressed north towards Bow River Campground near the intersection of FS100 and FS101. The end point was marked at the north end of a concentrated area of tree debris, small tree uprooting, and dislodged branches at an elevation around 9000 feet.||It should be noted that sporadic tree damage was also noted both southwest and northwest of the main track and the concentrated damage area. Sporadic softwood pine uprooting was noted along FS100 just north of HWY 130, but showed no conclusive evidence of a converging pattern. Likewise, FS105, FS120, and FS111 also had sporadic trees down, but once again, all trees fell in a northerly direction. The uniform direction suggested straight-line winds were the likely culprit of this tree damage.

The Mullen Fire began on Thursday, September 17th in dense timber both litter and understory in the Medicine Bow National Forest under ideal fire weather conditions of low humidity, gusty winds, and critical fuel levels. Plenty of downed trees and recent beetle kill made the area a tinder box as several days through the end of September met Red Flag Warning conditions for critical fire weather and saw extreme growth for the fire to grow over 106,000 acres by the end of September. For communities of lower Keystone, Lake Creek and Foxborough, twenty-nine dwellings and thirty-one outbuildings were lost to the fire. On the last day of September extreme fire growth spread the fire down into Colorado. The fire continued to burn into October and November. Sixty-six total structures including homes and outbuildings were destroyed from the wildfire. Overall fire fighting cost $42.4 million.

The Mullen Fire continued to burn across the Medicine Bow National Forest through the month of October. Several late season Red Flag Warnings were issued for the zone for critical fire weather conditions that led to the wildfire spreading into Colorado at the end of September. Moderate to heavy snow occurred over the Sierra Madre mountains with the heaviest snow observed mainly above 9000 feet elevation. Precipitation accumulation data suggests the heaviest precipitation fell late on the 16th into the early morning hours on the 17th.

Snow Water Equivalent values of 0.5 inches with ratios near 20 to 1 suggest around 10 inches of snow at the Medicine Bow SNOTEL (Elevation 10,510 Feet). Precipitation accumulation data suggests the heaviest precipitation fell late on the 16th into the early morning hours on the 17th.

Multiple CoCoRaHS and official NWS observers reported 2-4 inches of snow in central and northwestern portions of Scotts Bluff County.

Multiple public and CoCoRaHS reports of 6 to 7 inches of snow in and around Douglas.
Numerous public and CoCoRaHS reports of 6-8 inches across eastern Platte County. Highest amounts near Wheatland.
